newsitem.title: USA: State Street sees revenue growth below Q2's.
newsitem.headline: State Street sees revenue growth below Q2's.

text.p: State Street Corp Chief Financial Officer Ron O'Kelley said Wednesday that the company will continue to have strong growth in revenues, but the second quarter will be difficult to match.
Revenues grew by 22 percent in the second quarter over the previous second quarter by $102 million to $568 million, well above the company's goal of 15 percent revenue growth.
"I don't think we'll continue at the 22 pct level, but we will continue to have strong growth...above the 15 pct goal," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

O'Kelley said the strong U.S. dollar has not impacted the company as negatively as some of State Street's competitors. In fact, volatility in worldwide currencies contributed to a 66 percent rise in foreign exchange trading revenues in the second quarter to $50 million, he said.
"We're less impacted by the strong dollar than I think other businesses may be. The volatility is the thing that makes our business interesting," he said.
